genesis.author: Moses (traditional)
genesis.setting: The book opens before time as we count it, with the creation in 4004 BC, and closes in Egypt with the death of Joseph in 1635 BC. Its scenes move from Eden and Mesopotamia to Canaan and Egypt.
genesis.summary: Genesis tells how God made the world and everything in it, how sin entered and spread, and how God began to rescue the world through one family. It follows Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph, and ends with Israel living in Egypt.
themes: God's faithfulness to a chosen family

outline.title: The fall, and the line to Noah
The flood and the tower of Babel

exodus.author: Moses (traditional)
exodus.setting: Israel is in Egypt, enslaved, from the birth of Moses in 1571 BC; the book ends at Mount Sinai in 1490 BC with the tabernacle set up. The scenes run from the Nile to the Red Sea and the wilderness.
exodus.summary: Exodus tells how God heard his people's cry, sent plagues on Egypt and brought Israel out through the sea. At Sinai he gave them the law and made his covenant with them, then came to live among them in the tabernacle.

outline.title: Bondage, Moses and the ten plagues
Out of Egypt and into the wilderness
The covenant and the law at Sinai
The golden calf and the covenant renewed
The tabernacle built and filled with glory

leviticus.author: Moses (traditional)
leviticus.setting: The book belongs to the year 1490 BC, while Israel camps at the foot of Mount Sinai. The Lord first speaks to Moses from the tabernacle that has just been set up.
leviticus.summary: Leviticus tells Israel how a sinful people may come near a holy God. It sets out the offerings, the work of the priests, the laws of clean and unclean, the Day of Atonement and the feasts, and calls the people to be holy as the Lord is holy.

outline.title: The Day of Atonement, and the life in the blood
The feasts and the sacred years

numbers.author: Moses (traditional)
numbers.setting: The story runs from the second year after the exodus, 1490 BC, at Sinai, through thirty-eight years in the wilderness, to the plains of Moab by the Jordan in 1451 BC.
numbers.summary: Numbers counts Israel and sets the camp in order, then tells how the people refused to enter the land and wandered for a generation. A new generation reaches the edge of Canaan, and the book closes with the land's borders, the cities of refuge and the inheritance of Zelophehad's daughters.
themes: God's patience with a grumbling people

outline.title: The census and the camp at Sinai
Complaints, the spies and the wandering
From Edom to Moab, and Balaam
Settlement east of the Jordan, and the borders

deuteronomy.author: Moses (traditional)
deuteronomy.setting: The book is set in the plains of Moab in 1451 BC, just before Israel crosses the Jordan. It is Moses' farewell, spoken in the last weeks of his life.
deuteronomy.summary: Moses speaks to the new generation, looking back over the forty years and restating the law before they enter the land. He calls them to love the Lord with all their heart, sets before them blessing and curse, and the book ends with his death.
themes: Love the Lord with all your heart
The choice of life or death

outline.title: Moses looks back on the wilderness
The commandments and the call to love God
The laws for life in the land
Joshua, the song and the death of Moses

joshua.author: Joshua (traditional)
joshua.written: about 1415 BC, after the death of Eleazar that closes it
joshua.setting: The events run from the crossing of the Jordan in 1451 BC to the death of Joshua in 1443 BC, and of Eleazar the priest after him. They take place across the land of Canaan.
joshua.summary: Under Joshua, Israel crosses the Jordan, takes Jericho and wins the land in battle. The country is then divided among the tribes, and Joshua ends his life calling the people to serve the Lord.
themes: God keeps his promise of the land

outline.title: Crossing the Jordan and taking Jericho
The land divided among the tribes
The eastern tribes, and Joshua's farewell

judges.author: Samuel (traditional)
judges.setting: The book covers about 350 years, from the death of Joshua in 1443 BC to near the time of the first king, in 1095 BC. Israel lives in the land, tribe by tribe, without a king.
judges.summary: Again and again Israel turns from the Lord, falls under an enemy, cries out and is delivered by a judge. The cycle grows worse until the book ends in idolatry and civil war, with the refrain that there was no king in Israel.
themes: The cycle of sin and rescue
Every man did what was right in his own eyes

outline.title: Israel fails to finish the work
The judges, from Othniel to Samson

ruth.author: Unknown (Jewish tradition: Samuel)
ruth.setting: The story is set in the days when the judges ruled; the site places the birth of Obed about 1170 BC. It moves between Moab and Bethlehem.
ruth.summary: Naomi loses her husband and sons in Moab and returns to Bethlehem with her Moabite daughter-in-law Ruth. Ruth gleans in the field of Boaz, who redeems the family and marries her, and she becomes an ancestor of David.

outline.title: Loss, and the return to Bethlehem
The redeemer, and the line of David

1-samuel.author: Samuel, with Nathan and Gad (traditional)
1-samuel.setting: The book runs from the birth of Samuel about 1150 BC to the death of Saul in 1055 BC. Israel moves from judges to a king, and the scenes are Shiloh, Gibeah, the Valley of Elah and the wilderness of Judah.
1-samuel.summary: Samuel is born to Hannah and serves as prophet and judge. Israel asks for a king, Saul is chosen and then rejected, and David is anointed. David kills Goliath, is hunted by Saul, and the book ends with Saul's death.
themes: God rejects pride and lifts up the humble

outline.title: David and Goliath, and Saul's jealousy

2-samuel.author: Nathan and Gad (traditional)
2-samuel.setting: The book covers David's reign, from 1055 to 1017 BC. It begins at Ziklag and Hebron, moves to Jerusalem and ends with the plague of the census.
2-samuel.summary: David becomes king over Judah and then all Israel, takes Jerusalem and brings the ark there. God promises him a house and a throne for ever, but David's sin with Bathsheba brings trouble on his family, including the rebellion of Absalom.

outline.title: David king, first of Judah and then of all Israel
Jerusalem, the ark and the covenant
Songs, mighty men and the census

1-kings.author: Unknown (Jewish tradition: Jeremiah)
1-kings.setting: The book covers the years from 1015 to 896 BC: the end of David, the reign of Solomon, the split of the kingdom and the days of Elijah and Ahab.
1-kings.summary: Solomon receives wisdom, builds the temple and then turns his heart to other gods. The kingdom divides into Israel and Judah, and the prophet Elijah stands against Ahab and Baal.

2-kings.author: Unknown (Jewish tradition: Jeremiah)
2-kings.setting: The book covers about 330 years, from 896 BC to Jehoiachin's release from prison in 562 BC, with the fall of Jerusalem in 588 BC between. Israel falls to Assyria, and Judah later falls to Babylon.
2-kings.summary: Elijah is taken up and Elisha carries on his work. The northern kingdom sinks into idolatry and is carried away by Assyria, and Judah, despite the reforms of Hezekiah and Josiah, is finally carried away to Babylon.

outline.title: Elijah taken up, and the ministry of Elisha
Athaliah, Joash and the kings to Ahaz

1-chronicles.author: Ezra (traditional)
1-chronicles.setting: The book reaches from Adam in its opening genealogies to the death of David and the crowning of Solomon in 1015 BC. It was written for Israel after the exile, to remind them of their roots.
1-chronicles.summary: After a long set of family lines from Adam, the book gives the story of David, with his reign cast in a hopeful light. It dwells on the ark, the covenant and David's preparations for the temple.

outline.title: David made king over all Israel
God's promise, David's wars and the census
Preparing the temple, and Solomon crowned

2-chronicles.author: Ezra (traditional)
2-chronicles.setting: The book runs from the start of Solomon's reign in 1015 BC to the decree of Cyrus in 537 BC, ending with the exile and the call to return.
2-chronicles.summary: Solomon builds the temple, and then the book follows the kings of Judah, praising those who sought the Lord and recording the cost of those who did not. It closes with Jerusalem burned and then with Cyrus's decree to rebuild.

ezra.author: Ezra (traditional)
ezra.setting: The book covers the return from Babylon, from the decree of Cyrus in 537 BC and the return under Zerubbabel in 536 BC to Ezra's coming to Jerusalem in 458 BC and his reform, finished in the spring of 457 BC, in the Persian Empire.
ezra.summary: The exiles return under Zerubbabel, rebuild the altar and the temple despite opposition, and complete it. Decades later Ezra comes to Jerusalem, teaches the law and leads the people to put away their disobedience.

outline.title: The return and the rebuilding of the temple
Ezra comes to Jerusalem and leads reform

nehemiah.author: Nehemiah, traditionally with Ezra
nehemiah.setting: The book belongs to the years 445 to 433 BC, in Persia and in Jerusalem under the Persian king Artaxerxes.
nehemiah.summary: Nehemiah, the king's cupbearer, hears that Jerusalem's walls are broken and asks leave to rebuild them. He finishes the wall in the face of opposition, and Ezra reads the law to a people who renew their covenant.
themes: The word of God read and kept

outline.title: The law read and the covenant renewed

esther.author: Unknown (Jewish tradition: Mordecai)
esther.setting: The story is set in the Persian capital, Susa, in the reign of Ahasuerus (the site follows the view that he is Xerxes I), between 483 and 473 BC.
esther.summary: Esther, a Jewish orphan, becomes queen of Persia. When Haman plots to destroy the Jews, she risks her life by going to the king, and the plot is turned back on Haman.

outline.title: Deliverance and the feast of Purim

job.author: Unknown (traditionally Job or Moses)
job.written: unknown; not before Job's death about 1495 BC, which it records; the events about 1635 BC
job.setting: Job lived in the land of Uz, in the age of the patriarchs; the site follows Ussher in placing his trials about 1635 BC, before Moses. The book is set in his home, on the ash heap and in the whirlwind.
job.summary: Job loses his children, his wealth and his health, though he is blameless. His friends say it must be his sin, Job protests his innocence and asks for an answer, and God answers him from the whirlwind and restores him.
themes: The wisdom and power of God

outline.title: The Lord answers, and Job is restored

psalms.author: David, Asaph, the sons of Korah, Solomon, Heman, Ethan and Moses (named in the headings), and others unnamed
psalms.written: about 1451 to 450 BC; many about 1015 BC
psalms.setting: The psalms were written over about a thousand years, from Moses (Psalm 90) to the years after the exile. David wrote nearly half of them, some, their headings say, in the wilderness, in a cave and in flight from Saul and from Absalom.
psalms.summary: The Psalms are Israel's prayers and songs: praise, thanksgiving, lament, confession and trust. They are gathered in five books, and many look ahead to the Messiah.

proverbs.author: Solomon, with sayings of the wise, of Agur and of King Lemuel
proverbs.setting: Most of the book comes from the reign of Solomon, about 1015 to 975 BC, and some sayings were copied out in the time of Hezekiah, about 700 BC.
proverbs.summary: Proverbs gathers short sayings that teach wisdom for daily life: work, speech, money, family and justice. It begins with a father's call to his son and ends with a portrait of a woman who fears the Lord.

outline.title: The sayings of Solomon and the wise
More proverbs of Solomon, copied under Hezekiah
Agur, Lemuel and the woman of worth

ecclesiastes.author: The Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem (traditionally Solomon)
ecclesiastes.setting: Tradition places the book late in the reign of Solomon, about 985 BC, when he looked back on a life of wealth and pleasure.
ecclesiastes.summary: The Preacher searches for meaning in wisdom, pleasure, work and riches and finds them empty if they are all there is. His conclusion is to fear God and keep his commandments, and to enjoy his gifts while we have them.
themes: The gift of work and of joy

outline.title: Live boldly and remember your Creator

song-of-solomon.author: Solomon
song-of-solomon.setting: The song is traditionally dated to the early reign of Solomon, about 1005 BC, and is set in the countryside and the royal city.
song-of-solomon.summary: A bride and her beloved speak to each other and about each other in poems of desire and delight. The book celebrates married love as a gift of God.

isaiah.author: Isaiah, the son of Amoz
isaiah.written: about 700 BC; finished after Sennacherib's death in 681 BC, which it records (Isaiah 37:38)
isaiah.setting: Isaiah prophesied in Jerusalem in the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; his vision of the Lord came in the year Uzziah died, 759 BC. These were the days of the Assyrian threat.
isaiah.summary: Isaiah warns Judah of judgment for injustice and idolatry, and speaks of a coming king and servant who will bring salvation. The last chapters speak comfort to a people who will go into exile and promise new heavens and a new earth.

outline.title: The Lord's judgment and triumph over the earth
Woes, and hope in the Assyrian crisis
Comfort for the exiles; the Lord above the idols
The Servant and the restoration of Zion
The new heavens and the new earth

jeremiah.author: Jeremiah, with Baruch his scribe
jeremiah.written: about 585 BC; finished after 562 BC with the last chapter (Jeremiah 52)
jeremiah.setting: Jeremiah's ministry begins in 629 BC in the reign of Josiah and runs through the fall of Jerusalem to Babylon in 588 BC and the years after, in Judah and Egypt.
jeremiah.summary: Jeremiah warns a people who will not listen that Babylon is coming, and is persecuted for it. He also promises that God will make a new covenant with his people and bring them home.

outline.title: The prophet called, and the first warnings
The broken covenant, the potter and the persecution of Jeremiah
Kings, false prophets and the letter to the exiles
The book of consolation and the new covenant
The siege, the fall and the flight to Egypt

lamentations.author: Jeremiah (traditional)
lamentations.setting: The poems were written after Jerusalem fell to Babylon in 588 BC, among the ruins of the city.
lamentations.summary: Five poems mourn the destruction of Jerusalem and the suffering of its people, and own that it came from the Lord's judgment. In the middle, the poet holds to the Lord's steadfast mercy.

ezekiel.author: Ezekiel, the son of Buzi, a priest
ezekiel.setting: Ezekiel was carried to Babylon in 599 BC and prophesied among the exiles by the river Chebar from 595 to 573 BC.
ezekiel.summary: Ezekiel sees the glory of God and is sent to warn the exiles that Jerusalem will fall. After it falls, he promises a new heart, the bones that live again, and a new temple where the Lord dwells.

outline.title: The vision of glory and the prophet's call

daniel.author: Daniel
daniel.setting: Daniel was taken to Babylon as a youth in 607 BC and served there under Nebuchadnezzar, Belshazzar, Darius and Cyrus. His last vision is dated in the third year of Cyrus, 535 BC.
daniel.summary: Daniel and his friends stay faithful in the courts of foreign kings and are delivered from the furnace and the lions' den. Daniel is given visions of empires that rise and fall and of a kingdom that God will set up for ever.

outline.title: Daniel in Babylon, and the king's dream
Visions of beasts, the ram and goat, and the seventy weeks

hosea.author: Hosea, the son of Beeri
hosea.setting: Hosea prophesied in the northern kingdom of Israel from about 785 BC, in the reign of Jeroboam II, into the days of Hezekiah, in its last decades before Assyria carried it away in 721 BC.
hosea.summary: God tells Hosea to marry an unfaithful wife, as a picture of Israel's unfaithfulness to the Lord. The book charges Israel with idolatry and calls it to return, for God's love will not let go.

outline.title: God's love, and the call to return

joel.author: Joel, the son of Pethuel
joel.setting: The book names no king; the site follows Ussher in placing Joel in Judah about 808 BC, early in the reign of Uzziah, when a plague of locusts had stripped the land.
joel.summary: A swarm of locusts becomes a picture of the day of the Lord. Joel calls the people to turn to God, and promises that he will pour out his Spirit on all flesh.

outline.title: Return to the Lord, and the Spirit poured out
The nations judged, and Zion blessed

amos.author: Amos, a herdman of Tekoa
amos.setting: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa in Judah, prophesied in the northern kingdom about 787 BC, in the prosperous reign of Jeroboam II.
amos.summary: Amos condemns the nations around Israel and then Israel itself for oppressing the poor and for empty worship. He closes with the promise that God will rebuild David's fallen tent.

outline.title: Judgment on the nations and on Israel
Visions of judgment, and the promise of restoration

obadiah.author: Obadiah
obadiah.setting: The prophecy is set about 588 BC, after Jerusalem fell to Babylon, when Edom gloated over the disaster.
obadiah.summary: Obadiah tells Edom, the descendants of Esau, that its pride will be brought down because it stood by when Jacob's people were attacked. He closes with the promise that the kingdom will be the Lord's.

outline.title: The day of the Lord, and Zion delivered

jonah.author: Jonah (traditional)
jonah.setting: Jonah prophesied in the days of Jeroboam II, and was sent to Nineveh, the capital of Assyria; the site follows Ussher in placing the mission about 771 BC.
jonah.summary: God sends Jonah to Nineveh, but he flees by sea and is swallowed by a great fish. After Jonah preaches there, the city repents, and Jonah is angry that God shows it mercy.

micah.author: Micah the Morasthite
micah.setting: Micah prophesied in Judah about 759 to 698 BC, in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, when Assyria was rising.
micah.summary: Micah rebukes rulers and false prophets who oppress the poor and warns of judgment on Samaria and Jerusalem. He speaks of a ruler to be born in Bethlehem and of what the Lord requires.

outline.title: Against grasping rulers and false prophets
The mountain of the Lord and the ruler from Bethlehem
What the Lord requires, and his pardon

nahum.author: Nahum the Elkoshite
nahum.setting: Nahum is dated about 660 BC, when Assyria was at the height of its power and its capital, Nineveh, seemed secure.
nahum.summary: Nahum announces that the Lord will bring down Nineveh for its cruelty. The same God is a refuge to those who trust him.

outline.title: The Lord is a jealous God

habakkuk.author: Habakkuk the prophet
habakkuk.setting: The book is set about 607 BC in Judah, as Babylon rose to power and threatened the land.
habakkuk.summary: Habakkuk asks why God lets wrong go unpunished and then why he would use Babylon to punish it. God answers that the righteous will live by faith, and the prophet ends by praising him whatever comes.

outline.title: The prophet's complaints and the Lord's answers
Woes, and the righteous who live by faith

zephaniah.author: Zephaniah, the son of Cushi
zephaniah.setting: Zephaniah prophesied in Judah in the reign of Josiah; the site follows Ussher in placing his warnings about 629 BC, with the call of Jeremiah and before the reform of 624 BC.
zephaniah.summary: Zephaniah warns of the day of the Lord that is coming on Judah and the nations. He ends with a promise that the Lord will gather a humble remnant and rejoice over them with singing.

outline.title: The day of the Lord on Judah
A call to seek the Lord, and judgment on the nations

haggai.author: Haggai the prophet
haggai.setting: Haggai spoke in Jerusalem in 520 BC, in the second year of Darius, to the returned exiles who had left the temple unfinished.
haggai.summary: Haggai calls the people to stop building their own houses and finish the temple. The Lord promises that the glory of this house will be greater and that he will bless them.

outline.title: The glory of the new house

zechariah.author: Zechariah, the son of Berechiah
zechariah.setting: Zechariah prophesied from 520 to 518 BC, beginning in the same year as Haggai, to the returned exiles in Jerusalem as they rebuilt the temple.
zechariah.summary: Zechariah sees a series of night visions of God's care for Jerusalem and calls the people back to the Lord. He foretells a humble king on a donkey, a pierced one, and the day when the Lord will be king over all the earth.

outline.title: Eight night visions and the crowning of Joshua
The coming king and the rejected shepherd
The pierced one, the cleansing and the reign of the Lord

malachi.author: Malachi
malachi.setting: Malachi is the last of the prophets, about 430 BC, in Jerusalem after the temple was rebuilt and Nehemiah's reforms.
malachi.summary: Malachi speaks to a people who have grown careless in worship and faithless in marriage and giving. He promises a messenger who will prepare the way and the coming of the Lord to his temple.
themes: The messenger and the day of the Lord

matthew.author: Matthew, also called Levi, an apostle (traditional)
matthew.setting: The book covers the life of Jesus from his birth, about 5 BC, to his resurrection and the Great Commission in AD 33, in Bethlehem, Galilee and Jerusalem.
matthew.summary: Matthew shows Jesus as the promised king, son of David and son of Abraham, the fulfilment of the Old Testament. He records the Sermon on the Mount, the parables of the kingdom, the cross and the empty tomb, and ends with Jesus sending his disciples to all nations.

outline.title: Authority and the mission of the Twelve
Opposition and the parables of the kingdom
Teaching the disciples on the way

mark.author: John Mark, from Peter's preaching (traditional)
mark.setting: The story covers the ministry of Jesus from his baptism, about AD 27, to his death and resurrection in AD 33, in Galilee, on the road and in Jerusalem.
mark.summary: Mark moves quickly through the deeds of Jesus, the servant who gives his life as a ransom for many. More than a third of the book is the last week in Jerusalem.
themes: Jesus the Son of God and servant
The secret and the open confession

outline.title: The transfiguration and the road to Jerusalem

luke.author: Luke, the physician and companion of Paul (traditional)
luke.setting: The book runs from the promise of the birth of John the Baptist, about 6 BC, to the resurrection and ascension in AD 33, in Galilee, Samaria, Judea and Jerusalem.
luke.summary: Luke writes an orderly account for Theophilus, with a care for the poor, the outcast and women. It holds many parables found only in this Gospel, such as the good Samaritan and the prodigal son.

outline.title: The births of John and Jesus

john.author: The disciple whom Jesus loved (traditionally John the apostle)
john.setting: The book covers the ministry of Jesus from about AD 27 to his resurrection in AD 33, moving between Galilee and Jerusalem at the feasts.
john.summary: John opens with the Word who was with God and became flesh, and tells of seven signs and Jesus' claims to be the bread of life, the light and the good shepherd. It was written that readers might believe that Jesus is the Christ and have life in his name.

outline.title: The first signs and the new birth
Signs, the bread of life and the good shepherd

acts.author: Luke (traditional)
acts.setting: Acts runs from the ascension in AD 33 to Paul's two years of house arrest in Rome, AD 63 to 65, across Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, Asia Minor, Greece and Rome.
acts.summary: Acts tells how the Holy Spirit came at Pentecost and how the message of Jesus spread from Jerusalem to Rome. It follows Peter and then Paul, through missionary journeys, councils, arrests and trials.
themes: Witness to the ends of the earth

outline.title: The gospel reaches Samaria and the Gentiles
The third journey, Ephesus and Miletus

romans.author: Paul, the apostle
romans.setting: Paul wrote from Corinth in AD 60, at the end of his third journey, to the church in Rome, which he had not yet visited.
romans.summary: Romans sets out the gospel: all have sinned, and God puts people right with himself by faith in Christ. It goes on to life in the Spirit, God's purpose for Israel, and the way of life that follows.

outline.title: All have sinned; righteousness by faith
Dead to sin, alive in the Spirit

1-corinthians.author: Paul, the apostle
1-corinthians.setting: Paul wrote from Ephesus in AD 59 to the church in Corinth, a busy, divided Greek port city.
1-corinthians.summary: Paul answers reports and questions from Corinth about divisions, immorality, marriage, food offered to idols, worship and spiritual gifts. He lifts the whole discussion with the chapter on love and the chapter on the resurrection.

outline.title: Food offered to idols, and freedom
Worship, the Lord's supper, gifts and love

2-corinthians.author: Paul, the apostle
2-corinthians.setting: Paul wrote from Macedonia in AD 60, after Titus brought news that Corinth had responded to his earlier letter.
2-corinthians.summary: Paul writes of the comfort God gives in affliction and the ministry of reconciliation. He urges generous giving to the poor in Jerusalem and defends his apostleship against critics.

outline.title: Comfort, forgiveness and the ministry of the new covenant

galatians.author: Paul, the apostle
galatians.setting: Paul wrote about AD 58, on his third journey, soon after passing through Galatia again, to the churches of Galatia in Asia Minor.
galatians.summary: Paul writes against those who said Gentile believers must keep the law of Moses. People are justified by faith in Christ, not by works of the law, and are called to live free by the Spirit.

ephesians.author: Paul, the apostle
ephesians.setting: Paul wrote about AD 64 from prison in Rome to the believers in Ephesus.
ephesians.summary: Paul praises God for the blessings given in Christ and for the one new people formed of Jew and Gentile. The second half calls the church to live worthy of this calling in unity, holiness, family life and spiritual battle.

outline.title: What God has done in Christ
Households and the armour of God

philippians.author: Paul, the apostle
philippians.setting: Paul wrote about AD 64 from prison in Rome to the church in Philippi, which he had founded on his second journey.
philippians.summary: Paul thanks the Philippians for their gifts and writes with joy from prison. He holds up the humility of Christ and urges them to press on toward the prize.

outline.title: Rejoice, and the God of peace

colossians.author: Paul, the apostle
colossians.setting: Paul wrote about AD 64 from prison in Rome to the church in Colossae in Asia Minor.
colossians.summary: Paul answers false teaching by showing that Christ is supreme over all creation and that believers are complete in him. He then describes what the new life in Christ looks like at home and at work.

outline.title: The supremacy of Christ, and warnings
The new life, and final greetings

1-thessalonians.author: Paul, the apostle
1-thessalonians.setting: Paul wrote about AD 54 from Corinth, soon after founding the church in Thessalonica on his second journey.
1-thessalonians.summary: Paul gives thanks for the Thessalonians' faith and reminds them of his time with them. He encourages them to live holy lives and comforts them about those who have died, with the promise of the Lord's return.

outline.title: Holy living and the Lord's coming

2-thessalonians.author: Paul, the apostle
2-thessalonians.setting: Paul wrote about AD 55 from Corinth, not long after the first letter.
2-thessalonians.summary: Paul encourages believers who were suffering and corrects a mistaken idea that the day of the Lord had already come. He tells them to stand firm and to keep working.

1-timothy.author: Paul, the apostle
1-timothy.setting: Paul wrote about AD 65 to Timothy, his younger colleague, who was serving the church in Ephesus.
1-timothy.summary: Paul gives Timothy guidance on sound teaching, prayer and worship, and the qualifications for overseers and deacons. He warns against false teaching and the love of money.

outline.title: Sound doctrine, prayer and church leaders
Care for widows and elders, and the true riches

2-timothy.author: Paul, the apostle
2-timothy.setting: Paul wrote about AD 66 from a Roman prison, expecting death, to Timothy in Ephesus. It is the last of his letters.
2-timothy.summary: Paul urges Timothy to be strong, to keep the gospel he has received and to endure hardship. He says that Scripture is God-breathed, and he looks to the crown waiting for him.

outline.title: Be strong and do not be ashamed
The last days, and Paul's last words

titus.author: Paul, the apostle
titus.setting: Paul wrote about AD 65 to Titus, whom he had left on the island of Crete to set the churches in order.
titus.summary: Paul tells Titus to appoint elders, teach sound doctrine and encourage good works. He rests everything on God's grace that brings salvation.

philemon.author: Paul, the apostle
philemon.setting: Paul wrote about AD 64 from prison in Rome to Philemon, a believer in Colossae.
philemon.summary: Paul sends the runaway slave Onesimus back to his master Philemon and asks him to receive him as a brother. It is a short, personal letter about forgiveness.

outline.title: Welcome him as you would welcome me

hebrews.author: Unknown (traditionally Paul)
hebrews.setting: The letter was written about AD 64 to Jewish believers tempted to turn back, before the temple fell in AD 70.
hebrews.summary: Hebrews shows that Jesus is greater than the angels, Moses and the priests of the old covenant. He is the high priest who has made the one perfect sacrifice, so the readers should hold on in faith.
themes: The high priest and the sacrifice

outline.title: The Son is greater than the angels
Greater than Moses; the rest of God
The high priest after the order of Melchizedek
The new covenant and the one sacrifice
Run with endurance, and live for God

james.author: James (traditionally the brother of Jesus)
james.setting: James wrote about AD 49, perhaps the earliest of the letters, to Jewish believers scattered abroad.
james.summary: James writes of faith that shows itself in works: patience in trials, control of the tongue, care for the poor, and prayer. It is practical wisdom for daily life.

1-peter.author: Peter, the apostle
1-peter.setting: Peter wrote about AD 64, probably from Rome, to believers scattered across Asia Minor who faced growing hostility.
1-peter.summary: Peter encourages believers who suffer, pointing to the living hope given through Christ's resurrection. He calls them to holy lives, to follow Christ's example in suffering, and to elders to shepherd the flock.

outline.title: A living hope and a chosen people
Shepherd the flock and stand firm

2-peter.author: Peter, the apostle
2-peter.setting: Peter wrote about AD 66 shortly before his death, to the same circle of churches.
2-peter.summary: Peter urges his readers to grow in the knowledge of Christ, warns against false teachers and answers those who mock that the Lord will not return. The Lord is patient, and the day will come.

1-john.author: John, the apostle (traditional)
1-john.setting: John wrote about AD 90, traditionally from Ephesus, to churches troubled by teachers who denied that Jesus came in the flesh.
1-john.summary: John gives tests by which believers may know that they have eternal life: walking in the light, obeying Christ, loving one another and holding to the truth about Jesus. God is light and God is love.

2-john.author: The elder (traditionally John the apostle)
2-john.setting: The elder wrote about AD 90 to the elect lady and her children, most likely a church and its members.
2-john.summary: The elder urges walking in truth and love and warns the church not to welcome teachers who deny that Jesus has come in the flesh.

3-john.author: The elder (traditionally John the apostle)
3-john.setting: The elder wrote about AD 90 to Gaius, a believer who showed hospitality to travelling teachers.
3-john.summary: The elder commends Gaius for welcoming the brothers and warns of Diotrephes, who refuses them. He speaks well of Demetrius.

jude.author: Jude, the brother of James (traditionally also a brother of Jesus)
jude.setting: Jude wrote about AD 65 to believers faced with false teachers who had slipped into the churches.
jude.summary: Jude urges his readers to contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He warns with examples of judgment and ends with a doxology to the God who is able to keep them from falling.

outline.title: Keep yourselves in the love of God

revelation.author: John (traditionally the apostle)
revelation.setting: John received the visions on the island of Patmos about AD 95, and wrote to seven churches in Asia, some of them facing persecution.
revelation.summary: Revelation shows Jesus Christ in glory and sends letters to seven churches. Through visions of seals, trumpets and bowls it shows the struggle with evil and ends with the Lamb's victory and the new heaven and new earth.

outline.title: The vision of Christ, and the seven churches
The dragon, the beasts and the Lamb
The fall of Babylon, and the rider on the white horse
The thousand years and the judgment
The new heaven and the new earth
